## TL;DR

A handoff that reached its commit step while the engineer's own `repoos check` still held the check-gate lock failed at once with `A check is running; wait for it to finish.` The commit step now waits for the lock, polling once a second for up to 45 minutes, and proceeds when it clears. Stale or dead-holder locks are reconciled on every poll, so a crashed check never holds a handoff. The task shows `Waiting for the running check to finish` while it waits. The handoff fails only if the wait times out.

## Work and rationale

The refusal comes from the gate hook in `src/server/check-gate-lock.ts`, which `runGit` consults before every `git add`/`git commit`. `guardReviewTransition` in `src/server/review-guard.ts` is the handoff commit step: it runs `git add -A -- .` and then `git commit`, and turned that refusal into `git add failed: …`, so the handoff failed immediately.

I wrapped the guard rather than the individual git calls. The guard is documented as idempotent (a re-run after a successful commit passes without re-committing), so retrying the whole add-and-commit step is safe and avoids a second, partial retry path. The wait is a generic helper, `waitForCheckGateRelease`, which re-runs an attempt while a `held` predicate says the refusal is the only problem. It calls `recoverStaleCheckGateLocks` before each re-check, and it stops at a deadline. The default of 45 minutes matches the local check queue timeout already in config, so a check allowed to run that long is not cut short by its own waiter.

The guard matches the refusal text (`/A check is running/`) on its failure detail. That keeps the wait narrow: any other failure returns on the first attempt, unchanged.

For the visible state I reused the existing handoff-status progress. `setHandoffWaitingReason` writes a `reason` onto the running attempt only, and clears it after the wait. The drawer's progress label shows that reason ahead of its step-name fallback. I added a `reason` field to the UI `TaskCheckRun` type to match.

Docs: `docs/check-run-history.md` and `user-docs/check.md` describe the bounded wait, the waiting line, the 45-minute timeout and the stale-lock recovery.

## Approaches tried

First I tried releasing the test lock on a fixed 150 ms timer. The guard's first `git add` can run after that timer on a slow start, so the refusal never happened and the test failed with no wait. I replaced the timer with a release from `onCheckGateWait`, so the release happens only once the guard is actually waiting. That made the test deterministic.

## Challenges and blockers

Acceptance criterion 1 also covers "any other server git operation refused by the lock". I did not wrap every caller. The change covers the handoff commit step, which `guardReviewTransition` also serves for the `PATCH` route, but other refused writes still fail fast. Making those wait too would need the same wrapper at each call site, and it is a separate decision. I have not filed a follow-up task for it.

I did not verify the drawer label in a browser. The change is a one-line label precedence, and the scoped check's UI smoke test is the only browser coverage here.

## Key learnings

Only the refusal text should trigger a wait. A broad retry on any git failure would hide real errors behind a 45-minute delay. Tying test timing to the observable event (the wait starting) is more reliable than a fixed sleep, because the guard's startup cost varies with machine load.
